idiom_name: mapper module over a Hash or Data.define message; JSON.generate/JSON.parse at the endpoint
implementation_notes: Ruby's idiom is a module with two class methods - OrderMessageMapper.to_message(order) and .from_message(payload) - over a message that is either a plain Hash of wire keys (with JSON.generate/JSON.parse owning the wire half) or a Data.define value object when the shape deserves a type. Hash#slice, transform_keys and dig do the mechanical half, and the mapper is the only file that knows both the message keys and the aggregate's attributes; as_json/ActiveSupport is the shortcut to avoid, because it moves the wire shape onto the domain model instead of keeping it in the mapper.
code_sketch:
OrderMessage = Data.define(:id, :customer_id, :total_minor)

module OrderMessageMapper                      # both directions, one file
  def self.to_message(o)
    OrderMessage.new(id: o.id, customer_id: o.customer.id, total_minor: o.total.minor_units)
  end

  def self.from_message(m)                     # m: Hash or OrderMessage
    Order.rehydrate(m.fetch(:id), m.fetch(:customer_id), Money.minor(m.fetch(:total_minor)))
  end
end
# endpoint: producer.publish(JSON.generate(OrderMessageMapper.to_message(o).to_h))
pitfalls: String-keyed and symbol-keyed messages are the classic Ruby messaging bug (m[:id] versus m['id']): pin one key style in the mapper or normalise with transform_keys.
Monkey-patching to_json/as_json onto the domain class leaks the wire shape into the model and hides the mapping from review.
Data.define instances are frozen but their members are not deep-frozen: a message holding an array still lets a consumer mutate it.
fetch raises on a missing key while [] returns nil - choose per field, but never let nil silently become a default downstream.
